answer: Ephemeral kernel attestation. Each agent gets a short-lived kernel hash tied to its current task; every clone must re-derive a fresh hash through 30+ seconds of sequential memory-hard work, or its fable (declared task history) fails verification and its actions are dropped. Honest agents amortize one derivation across a long task; a sybil operator pays that work per clone per cycle, so cloning N identities costs N times the derivation latency, while a single honest identity pays it once. A prism check cross-links hashes to prior work, blocking reuse.
